title: The house that cost one dollar
excerpt: The cost of reaching a given level of performance with AI is falling by a factor of 13 per year. If a million-dollar house fell at the same pace it would cost $455 after three years — and one dollar after five. Which is why bans are the wrong question for schools.

title: Your custom GPT or Gem is changing shape
excerpt: OpenAI is retiring custom GPTs and Google is replacing Gems with skills. Your instructions and your files carry across. The sharing links, the permissions and the chat history do not — and that is the part schools should act on.

title: What are the consequences when the copy is free?
excerpt: Seven Adobe applications were cloned in a week by eight AI agents. Adobe's share price barely moved, because the market had already repriced the threat. What cheap imitation actually changes, for the software industry and for the people in it.

title: Evidence you can interrogate — introducing the Evidence Toolkit
excerpt: A new reference page where every effect size is hand-verified against a named meta-analysis — and where any claim, ours or anyone else's, can be interrogated in your chatbot.

title: Why I built choosewise.education
excerpt: A new site, a new framework, and a stack of free, practical material for the people who actually run schools.
